poster_title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Obscures Hallucination Cues in Large Language Models: An Empirical Evaluation
authors: Jiahao Cheng, Tiancheng Su, Jia Yuan, Guoxiu He, Jiawei Liu, Xinqi Tao, Jingwen Xie, Huaxia Li
paper_info: East China Normal University, Wuhan University, Xiaohongshu Inc., 2025

content: LLMs have shown remarkable performance in NLP tasks.
However, they may generate factually incorrect or irrelevant content.
Hallucination detection methods rely on output consistency, internal states, and self-evaluation.
CoT prompting helps reduce hallucinations but its impact on detection is under-explored.
CoT may obscure critical signals used for hallucination detection.
Conducted pilot experiments on MCQA tasks using CommonSenseQA, ARC-Challenge, and MMLU datasets.
Used three LLMs: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-v0.3-Instruct, and Deepseek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B.
Evaluated on complex fact-based datasets: TriviaQA, PopQA, HaluEval, and TruthfulQA.
CoT prompting significantly alters the probability distribution of final answer tokens, making hallucinations more plausible.
panels.figure_caption: Qualitative results of the proposed method

content: Advanced detection methods lose their typical advantage over perplexity-based baselines under CoT prompting.
CoT prompting improves LLM performance but disrupts hallucination detection mechanisms.
Reasoning-enhanced inference reshapes the landscape of hallucination detection.
